headline: Microsoft launches new Nvidia RTX Spark AI PCs starting at $2,599, with 1 petaflop Dev Box
summary: Microsoft's new Surface Laptop Ultra and RTX Spark Dev Box, powered by Nvidia's new SoC, offer significant local AI compute and unified memory. Pre-orders are live, with devices shipping October 16.
details: Microsoft officially unveiled its new Surface Laptop Ultra, powered by the Nvidia RTX Spark SoC, starting at $2,599. It features a 5120- or 6144-core Blackwell GPU and up to 128GB LPDDR5x unified memory, shipping October 16.

Also announced was the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, an anodized aluminum unit priced at $5,999. This developer-focused machine boasts 1 petaflop of AI compute performance and comes with a custom Windows 11 build optimized for AI.

The hardware leverages unified memory to dynamically allocate resources for tasks like modern gaming and local AI development. Gears of War: E-Day was demonstrated running on the system, highlighting its graphical capabilities.

Beyond hardware, Microsoft detailed significant updates for Windows 11, including an overhauled Copilot. This new version will enable system-level tasks directly from the search bar, simplifying user interactions.

To address security concerns with AI agents, Microsoft introduced Execution Containers (MXC). This framework allows developers and organizations to sandbox agent activities and set guardrails, ensuring controlled access.
MXC supports various isolation backends, from process containers to experimental hardware-backed MicroVMs. This provides a robust policy layer for managing compute traffic and agent behavior.

Microsoft's "Hybrid Intelligence" concept emphasizes local AI solutions over cloud-backed ones. This allows users to allocate memory for specific applications and supports local frameworks like llama.cpp and models from Deepseek and Nvidia Nemotron families.

headline_marked: [[BMW iX4 SUV boasts 428 miles range]], starting at $66,200, launching March 2027
headline: BMW iX4 SUV boasts 428 miles range, starting at $66,200, launching March 2027
summary: The iX4 50 xDrive starts at $66,200, features an 800-volt architecture for fast charging, and delivers 463 horsepower, aiming to compete in the global EV market.
details: The BMW iX4, a coupe-shaped electric SUV, is the third vehicle on the new Neue Klasse platform. The iX4 50 xDrive will launch in March 2027, starting at $66,200 (excluding fees). It features a Gen6 high-voltage battery with 112.2kWh usable energy and an 800-volt architecture.

The iX4 boasts up to 428 miles of EPA-estimated range, exceeding the Tesla Model Y. BMW emphasizes range and efficiency as key selling points, positioning its new lineup against increasing competition from Chinese EV imports.

Performance is also a focus, with the iX4 50 xDrive delivering 463 horsepower and 475lb-ft of torque, achieving 0-60mph in 4.7 seconds. A more powerful M60 xDrive version will follow, offering 603hp and 645lb-ft of torque, with a 0-60 time a full second faster.

The Gen6 batteries use cylindrical lithium-ion cells, increasing energy density by 20% compared to previous prismatic cells. The "pack-to-open-body" construction integrates the battery housing into the vehicle's underbody, reducing weight and enhancing rigidity.

Its 800V architecture enables rapid charging, accepting up to 400kWs of DC fast charging to replenish 184 miles in just 10 minutes, or 10-80% charge in 21 minutes. The iX4 will also feature a NACS charging port for compatibility with Tesla Superchargers.

Inside, the Panoramic iDrive infotainment system replaces traditional gauges with a full-width heads-up projection on the lower windshield. A 17.9-inch central touchscreen allows for customizable widgets.
